name: Slévárna Vrbenský s.r.o.

quality.trend: perfect until 2025Q3; red now only because 2 porosity/burr QNs hit ~24 small lots (jumpy ppm). OTD still best-in-group.

payment_behaviour.note: avg 50.5 days on 45 net; 5.2 days late in last 12m

financial_health.signal: sound; has just invested in a new moulding line

notes: settled below its own ask every time (-5.9, 0.0, -1.7 %)

situation: Czech family foundry that has just doubled its stainless-casting capacity with a new automatic moulding line (news:20260420-09). The start-up ran over budget, and on 14 Oct its house bank cut the credit line (news:20261014-S11). It now asks customers to pay within 10 days from November to keep alloy material flowing (doc:20261016-70170-S12). It still needs volume, calls Hollerau an important reference customer, and is the cheaper HI 80-250 source (559.61 vs Allgäu-Reiter 654.52), yet holds only 25 %. Cash is now the main currency, ahead of volume and reference value; it has accepted cuts readily, and it promises a report on porosity corrective actions. Supply-security risk has risen, so any volume shift should be staged and tied to evidence of stable finances.

update_notes.summary: Vrbenský's house bank has cut its credit line after the new moulding line ran over budget, and the foundry now formally asks all customers to pay within 10 days from November. The cash pressure has become acute, so fast payment is now our strongest lever for price and porosity containment, but its financial-health and supply-security risk has risen. The foundry also promises corrective actions on porosity.
